I have a great plot idea stuck in my head, but I'm having a hard time creating a good character for the story. What are your tips for developing a good character?
How to Develop a Good Character?

An easy way to start is to use someone you know as a "status quo" for your character. Then you have a very clear idea how your character would react in millions of different situations, with all his/hers quirks, dislikes, odd preferences, old scars etc. and will end up with a well-rounded character. And as you weave this character into your fiction, it will soon enough become it's own character by how it interacts with the world and develops from there.

In order to keep your character interesting troughout the story, you could leech off of method acting. Crawl into the skin of your protagonist and use your own emotions to feel what drives your character in different situations.

There is also a big difference between plot-driven and character-driven stories. When you have a plot-driven story it doesn't really matter who your protagonist is, and he or she can be easily replaced by any other character (it can happen to anyone). Character-driven literature is usually more in-depth and interesting, because it relies heavy on character-development and makes for the more complex and interesting stories. Think up a reason why your story could have only happened to your character and how it effects him or her in the longer run. (i.e. Only Frodo could have destroyed the One Ring, because he is a hobbit (longing for simplicity and being light-hearted), this causes the Ring not to have such an effect on him. But the majority of Hobbits would never have been able to complete their quest, because Frodo is a particular adventure-loving and brave Hobbit, which runs in his family. These are very strict conditions that make sure that only due to Frodo's character this story can take place the way it does. (even though, LOTR is very plot-driven, the characters are also a big factor in the progression of the story)

I hope this info helped a little. Good luck writing!

I learned a few years ago in undergrad biology classes that the Smokey Bear campaign was actually one of the worst things to happen to North American forests in terms of wildfire prevention and habitat conservation, not to mention the damage to homes and local businesses. By preventing forest fires, forests accumulate dead plant material over time that would otherwise burn in small fires once every few years. Now, because there's so much detritus built up, forest fires in the southwest, along the Rockies, and in BC are much larger and more destructive than in the past. What's more, trees have actually evolved defenses against forest fires like secreting thick, resinous sap to protect the seeds within pinecones. These larger forest fires are strong enough to overwhelm these adaptations and prevent the re-growth of forests.

Long story short, you're right. People shouldn't prevent or supress smaller fires if they don't directly threaten people. Larger, more rampant fires are basically the result of people not knowing when to leave well enough alone (sometimes).
